Container.Name: ARK-Survival-Ascended
Container.Overview:
ARK: Survival Ascended dedicated server.
ASA ships Windows-only server binaries, so this container installs the Windows depot with SteamCMD and runs it under GE-Proton. Both SteamCMD and Proton are fetched on first start, so the image itself stays small.
Heads up before you start: the game files are roughly 60GB and the server wants a lot of RAM (16GB is a sensible floor for a vanilla map, more with mods or players). Put the appdata on an SSD or a cache pool, not on the array.
First boot downloads ~60GB and then builds a Proton prefix. Expect a long, quiet startup - check the logs rather than assuming it hung.
Config files are kept editable over SMB. A "config" shortcut is created at the top of the game files folder pointing at ShooterGame/Saved/Config/WindowsServer, so you can browse straight to it from Windows. Stop the container before editing - the server rewrites GameUserSettings.ini when it shuts down and will overwrite changes made while it is running.
Only 7777/udp needs forwarding at your router. The old 27015 query port is vestigial in ASA because server discovery goes through Epic Online Services rather than Steam. Forward RCON only if you administer from outside your LAN.

Config.Name: Game Port
Config.Description: Game traffic. This is the one that has to be forwarded.

Config.Name: Peer Port
Config.Description: Game port + 1. Not normally required, but cheap to forward if players report flaky connects.

Config.Name: Query Port
Config.Description: Legacy Steam query port. Vestigial in ASA - discovery runs through EOS. Left here for tooling that expects it.

Config.Name: RCON Port
Config.Description: Source RCON. Only forward at the router if you administer remotely, and never without a strong admin password.

Config.Name: Game Files
Config.Description: Where the ~60GB of server files, saves and configs live. Use a cache pool or SSD share.

Config.Name: SteamCMD
Config.Description: Shared SteamCMD install. Safe to point several game containers at the same folder.

Config.Name: Proton
Config.Description: GE-Proton build plus the wine prefix. Delete this folder to rebuild the prefix from scratch if the server starts misbehaving.

Config.Name: Server Name
Config.Description: Session name shown in the Unofficial server list.

Config.Name: Map
Config.Description: Note the _WP suffix - ASA maps are World Partition and the bare ASE name will not load. e.g. TheIsland_WP, ScorchedEarth_WP, TheCenter_WP, Aberration_WP, Extinction_WP, Ragnarok_WP, Astraeos_WP

Config.Name: Max Players
Config.Description: Passed as -WinLiveMaxPlayers. The old ?MaxPlayers= is ignored by ASA.

Config.Name: Server Password
Config.Description: Join password. Leave blank for an open server.

Config.Name: Admin Password
Config.Description: Admin password, and also the RCON password - ASA has no separate RCON credential. Change this from the default.

Config.Name: Mods
Config.Description: Comma separated CurseForge project IDs, no spaces. ASA mods come from CurseForge, not the Steam Workshop. Load order follows the list, leftmost first.

Config.Name: Crossplay
Config.Description: Set true to let Epic Games Store players join. Not on by default for self-hosted servers - this is the usual reason Epic players cannot find a server.

Config.Name: BattlEye
Config.Description: BattlEye does not run cleanly under Proton, so this defaults to false (which passes -NoBattlEye).

Config.Name: Extra Game Parameters
Config.Description: Extra dash flags, space separated. e.g. -ForceAllowCaveFlyers -servergamelog -NoTransferFromFiltering

Config.Name: Extra Query Parameters
Config.Description: Extra ?key=value pairs for the map string, no leading ?. e.g. AllowCrateSpawnsOnTopOfStructures=true?PreventDownloadSurvivors=false

Config.Name: Cluster ID
Config.Description: Set the same value on every server in a cluster to enable transfers. Leave blank for a standalone server.

Config.Name: Cluster Directory
Config.Description: Shared transfer folder. For a real cluster, map this to a path shared by all the containers.

Config.Name: Validate Files
Config.Description: Set to true to have SteamCMD verify every file on start. Slow - turn it back off once it has run.

Config.Name: Proton Version
Config.Description: latest, or a pinned tag like GE-Proton9-27. Pin it if a new Proton build ever breaks the server, or if GitHub API rate limits bite.

Config.Name: Stop Timeout
Config.Description: Seconds to wait for a graceful save-and-exit before force killing. Also raise Unraid's own container stop timeout to match.

Config.Name: Steam Username
Config.Description: Leave blank. The ASA server app downloads anonymously.

Config.Name: Steam Password
Config.Description: Leave blank. The ASA server app downloads anonymously.

Config.Name: UID
Config.Description: User ID. 99 is the Unraid default.

Config.Name: GID
Config.Description: Group ID. 100 is the Unraid default.

Config.Name: Fix Share Permissions
Config.Description: Keeps the Saved folder (configs and saves) readable and writable over SMB, so you can edit the ini files from a Windows PC. Runs on every start and again on shutdown. Set false only if you want to manage permissions yourself.

Config.Name: Config UMASK
Config.Description: umask applied to the Saved folder (configs and saves) when Fix Share Permissions is on. Leave blank to reuse the container UMASK, which is the usual choice. 000 = everyone can edit. 007 = owner and group only, which still works for Unraid SMB users since they belong to the users group. 022 = read-only for everyone but the owner. 077 = owner only.

Config.Name: Config Permissions
Config.Description: Optional escape hatch. A chmod expression such as g+rwX applied recursively to the Saved folder. Overrides Config UMASK when set. Leave blank unless you need something a umask cannot express.

Config.Name: Data Permissions
Config.Description: chmod applied to the top-level server files folder. 775 rather than 770 so an SMB client that is not the owner and not in the group can still traverse into it.

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: umask for files the server creates. 000 means new files land as 666 and new directories as 777, which keeps them editable over the share.
